key_insight: A 3D opto-electro-thermal COMSOL model shows that an n-ZnSe/p-SrScCu3Se4/p+-WSe2 heterostructure can achieve very high photovoltaic efficiency when absorber width, acceptor density, and defect levels are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a device-design blueprint for quaternary chalcogenide solar cells, showing how realistic 3D transport and heating effects should be managed to improve efficiency and thermal robustness.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and thermal loss under AM1.5G, 1-sun illumination
Parameter sweep of absorber width, acceptor level, and bulk defects
evidence_signal: Under optimized conditions, the device reaches VOC = 1.02 V, JSC = 32.472 mA/cm2, FF = 88.212%, and PCE = 29.217%, with QE strongest in the visible range and weaker in the near-infrared.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based, so real-device performance may differ due to fabrication defects, interface quality, and material parameter uncertainty.
paper_title: Computational analysis and performance optimization of SrScCu3Se4-based solar cells using COMSOL Multiphysics
